classification.difficultyReason: The hardest part requires independently splitting repeated-digit numbers into the disjoint patterns 2+1+1 and 2+2, then choosing digits and counting arrangements without double-counting. The other parts use routine position counting and a complement probability.

content.prompt: Four-digit numbers are to be formed from the digits 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

children.label: a
children.prompt: For each of the cases below, find how many four-digit numbers can be formed if:

children.label: i
children.prompt: any digit may appear up to four times in the number

answer.worked:
Each of the four positions has six choices.
$$N=6^4=1296.$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: no digit may appear more than once in the number

answer.worked:
The successive numbers of choices are 6, 5, 4 and 3.
$$N=6\times5\times4\times3=360.$$

children.label: iii
children.prompt: there is at least one repeated digit, but no digit appears more than twice in a number

answer.worked:
The disjoint patterns are one pair with two distinct single digits, or two pairs.

For one pair, choose its digit in 6 ways. Its positions can be $12,13,14,23,24$ or $34$: 6 choices. Fill the remaining positions from left to right with two different digits in $5\times4$ ways.
$$N_{2+1+1}=6\times6\times5\times4=720.$$

For two pairs, choose the two digits in $(6\times5)\div2=15$ ways; division by 2 removes the two orders of each digit pair. Place the smaller digit in one of the same six position pairs; the larger digit fills the other positions.
$$N_{2+2}=15\times6=90.$$
Thus $N=720+90=810$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the probability that a four-digit number chosen at random from the set of numbers in part a i contains at least one six.

answer.short:
$\frac{671}{1296}$

Subtract the probability of no sixes from 1.
answer.worked:
There are $6^4$ equally likely numbers. A number with no six has five choices at each position, giving $5^4$ numbers.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one six})&=1-\frac{5^4}{6^4}\\P(\text{at least one six})&=\frac{1296-625}{1296}\\P(\text{at least one six})&=\frac{671}{1296}\end{align*}$$
